1

  • N: ina pī (|) bibli || ina rēš (|) arhi
  • T: At the start of the New Moon, at the beginning of the month,
  • L: ina ← ina I “(im-m..., ip-p... etc.) in, on”; pī ← pû I “(also OB)”; bibli ← biblu I “pl. m. & f. the (action of) bringing”; ina ← ina I “(im-m..., ip-p... etc.) in, on”; rēš ← rēšu I “head”; arhi ← warhu I “”
  • Note: On the reading rēš arḫi, see [NABU1996-13]. According to [wasserman2020flood: 89], the line reflects the tradition that the Flood started when the moon was invisible (on which see [RN1780: 209–210]), present in the Old Babylonian version (OB II 439b: ana ūm warḫim, “by the day of the New Moon”), in the SB version (SB III 92: [... u₂-b]i-il ar-hu “[…] the month rea[ched its end],” and in MB Priv 50 ([... i-na u₄-mi-im] e#-ṭi#-i[m (x x x)], “[… on the] dimming [day]”). Unlike these traditions where the Flood starts on the new moon, Wasserman notes that this text presents the Flood as nearly finished on that date.
UgaMB1 o 1. i-na pi₂-i bi-ib-li i-na re-eš ITI

2

  • N: ēa | bēlu | rabû || ina šuttīya | izziza(m)-ma
  • T: Ea, the great lord, appeared to me in a dream,
  • L: ēa ← Ea I; bēlu ← bēlu I “lord”; rabû ← rabû I “big”; ina ← ina I “(im-m..., ip-p... etc.) in, on”; šuttīya ← šuttu I “pl. šunātu(m) dream š. naṭālu, amāru etc. to have a dream, to…”; izziza(m)-ma ← izuzzu I “to stand”
  • Note: The collation is reported in [NABU2008-70], where the reading of the word is also discussed.
UgaMB1 o 2-3a. {d}e₂-a be-lu GAL i-na MAŠ₂*.<GE₆>-ia | iz-zi-za-ma

3

  • N: liqē-ma | marra | u haṣṣinna
  • T: (Saying:) “Take a spade and a copper axe,
  • L: liqē-ma ← leqû II “to take, take over”; marra ← marru II “shovel, spade Bab. also as symbol of Marduk and Nabû”; u ← u I “and, but, also”; haṣṣinna ← haṣṣinnu I “Mari, NB pl. f. axe of copper, silver, gold etc.”
  • Note: Wasserman notes that the mention of a copper axe to carve a window suggests that hte boat is made of wood, and not of rope or reeds, as in other traditions ([wasserman2020flood: 89–90]).
UgaMB1 o 3b-4a. li-qe₂-ma {giš}mar-ra | u₃ ha-ṣi-in-na{urudu!}

4

  • N: apta | epuš | ana muhhi
  • T: “Open a window at the top,
  • L: apta ← aptu I “pl. apātu window, window opening Ass., O/jB in house, NB in sluice”; epuš ← epēšu II “to do”; ana ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; muhhi ← muhhu I “skull”
UgaMB1 o 4b-5a. ap-ta | e-pu-uš a-na muh-hi

5-6

  • N: uššir | iṣṣūram-ma || līmurakka | kibra
  • T: “Release a bird, that she find the shore for you!”
  • L: uššir ← wašāru I “~ to sink down”; iṣṣūram-ma ← iṣṣūru I “occas. f.”; līmurakka ← amāru I “to see”; kibra ← kibru I “pl. m. & f. bank, shore, rim of river, canal, sea, as safe place”
UgaMB1 o 5b-6. uš-ši-ir | MUŠEN-ma li-mu-rak-ka kib-ra

  • N: aqūl | anāku
  • T: I paid attention
  • L: aqūl ← qâlu I “to pay attention”; anāku ← anāku I “I”
UgaMB1 o 7a. a-qu-ul a-na-ku

8

  • N: ina qibīt(i) (|) ēa | bēlīya | māliki | rabî

UgaMB1 o 7b-8. i-na qi₂-bi-ti | {d}e₂-a be-li-ia ma-li-ki GAL

UgaMB1 o 9. al-qe₃-ma {giš}MAR u₃ ha-ṣi-na{urudu}

  • T: I opened a window at the top,
  • L: apta ← aptu I “pl. apātu window, window opening Ass., O/jB in house, NB in sluice”; ēpuš ← epēšu II “to do”; ana ← ana I “(aš-š... etc.) to, for (freq. abbr. an, with assimilation of n…”; muhhīya ← muhhu I “skull”

11

  • N: dannata | kappī | summata
  • T: Strong of wings, a dove
  • L: dannata ← dannu I “NA f. also da''atu strong, powerful, mighty, great of god, king,…”; kappī ← kappu I “wing O/jB of bird, ant, god, statue”; summata ← summatu I “(female) dove, pigeon”
UgaMB1 o 11. dan-na-ta kap-pi₂ su-ma-ta{mušen!}

12

  • N: umaššir | illik | itūram-ma
  • T: I released; she soared forth and returned to me.
  • L: umaššir ← wašāru I “~ to sink down”; illik ← alāku I “to go”; itūram-ma ← târu I “to turn, return”
  • Parallels: cf. L I.4 SB "XI" 148-150
UgaMB1 b.e. 1. u₂-maš-ši-ir il-lik i-tu₂-ra-ma

13

  • N: ušānih! | kappīša
  • T: She had exhausted her wings.
  • L: ušānih! ← anāhu I “to be(come) tired”; kappīša ← kappu I “wing O/jB of bird, ant, god, statue”
  • Note: A collation is reported in [NABU2008-70]; “u₂-ša-tik₂” (sic, presumably for tik). [cavigneaux2007oiseaux: 319] reads u₂-ša-ni-hi (“elle revint à bout de forces (litt. “elle avait épuisé ses ailes”)”; cf. also [darshan2021calendrical: 510]: “She exhausted her wings”); [RN88: 201] reads u₂-ša-kil₂ (“j’en avais exécuté artistiquement”). Wassermann ([wasserman2020flood: 90]) reads also u₂-ša-ni-ḫi instead of the expected ventive ušāniḫa.
UgaMB1 b.e. 2. u₂-ša-ni!-ih! kap-pi₂-ša

14

  • N: ašnī-ma | anāku || kumâ | umaššir-ma
  • T: Once again, I released a pelican.
  • L: ašnī-ma ← šanû III “to do twice, do for a second time”; anāku ← anāku I “I”; kumâ ← kumû I “(a water bird, phps.) pelican jB”; umaššir-ma ← wašāru I “~ to sink down”
  • Note: On the kumû-bird, see [cavigneaux2007oiseaux: 320]: “ce doit être un oiseau aquatique apte à se poser dans un terrain encore inondé, mais par une faible épaisseur d’eau.” [RN754: 24–243] and, following him, [wasserman2020flood: 90], identify the kumû bird as a crane (see also [darshan2021calendrical: 510], who identifies it as a “water-bird,” “perhaps a pelican”).
  • Note: The collation is reported in [NABU2008-70].
  • Parallels: cf. L I.4 SB "XI" 151
UgaMB1 r 1. aš-ni-ma a-na-ku ku-ma-a{mušen!(RI*)} u₂-ma-ši-ir-ma
